source.title: Twin-Boot: Uncertainty-Aware Optimization via Online Two-Sample Bootstrapping

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests a new uncertainty-driven regularizer and reports its effect on train/test performance and generalization gap, using a method different from the claim versions’ named interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a CIFAR-10 generalization-gap result and a synthetic seismic inverse-problem comparison. It does not test the listed versions’ specific interventions or conditions. Its cited results about other methods are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates Twin-Boot regularization and uncertainty estimation, but none of V1–V8. Its batch-size sweeps measure uncertainty rather than held-out performance, and its flatness argument does not test magnitude-aware sharpness against generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors present twin bootstrap trajectories and periodic mean-resets as an online local-uncertainty estimator whose weight sampling regularizes training. They report a reduced CIFAR-10 generalization gap, improved calibration, and lower seismic test loss and reconstruction error.
record.recipe_differences: Uses online two-sample bootstrapping, twin models, periodic mean-resets, and uncertainty-driven weight sampling; it is not the random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or memorized-example intervention specified in the versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper says the method is sensitive to reset schedule and cadence of weight sampling; toy-landscape uncertainty estimates are reported as largely invariant to learning rate and batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report a reduced CIFAR-10 training/validation accuracy gap with Twin-Boot relative to a baseline without its injected noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Twin-Boot can reduce the generalization gap in the reported VGG-16 CIFAR-10 setup.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report improved CIFAR-10 reliability curves with Twin-Boot.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Twin-Boot can improve predictive calibration in the reported CIFAR-10 setup.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 25 synthetic seismic-inversion seeds, Twin-Boot has higher training loss but lower test loss and reconstruction MSE than the standard optimizer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Twin-Boot improves held-out measurement fit and reconstruction accuracy in this synthetic inverse problem, while fitting training measurements less closely.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 accuracy and calibration evidence is presented in figures without numerical values or stated uncertainty. The seismic result is a synthetic inverse problem and does not establish performance on natural-label classification. The paper reports a single deep-network benchmark setup.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported qualifying result within the 60-row limit was omitted. Cited findings about prior methods were excluded.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error and their effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers under specified tuning regimes and recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations. Toy batch-size sweeps report uncertainty only.
Dropout effects, dataset-size dependence, underfitting, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and comparative ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because no row measures a listed version; this does not negate the reported method improvements. No version-level verdict is warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence; random-label test accuracy; named architectures and training recipes.
Width sweep past the interpolation threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning, weight decay, optimizer switching, and language-model results.
Large-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons, training-set-size regimes, underfitting, and dropout/weight-decay removal with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparison and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal and retraining of memorized examples and comparison with random-example removal.
